title: Charging a Payment Sent Back Unpaid on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan
content:
# Charging a Payment Sent Back Unpaid on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

**Finance desk servicing rule.** Where the bank sends a payment on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan back unpaid, the finance desk books a charge for that return against the plan's billing history, tied to the payment entry that came back. The charge goes on as a new positive entry carrying the returned-payment charge code and dated and cycled on today's date, so the customer will see it on the next statement; the plan's own balance record is left as it stands.

## Invoking `book_returned_payment_charge_6a9e81de`

The agent unlocks `book_returned_payment_charge_6a9e81de` and calls it. One call books a single charge for one return.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `financing_plan_id` | The reference number of the promotional financing plan record the charge is booked to | An identifier, read from the financing plan lookup for this customer before the call |
| `source_entry_id` | The reference number of the billing entry that records the payment the bank returned unpaid | An identifier, read from the plan's billing history lookup, where returned payments carry the returned outcome |
| `charge_amount` | The money charged for the returned payment | In USD as a positive number with 2 decimal places, half-up at the cent and with no currency symbol or thousands separator; an empty value is not accepted |

**Return.** A single confirmation sentence in plain text. It names the reference number minted for the new billing entry, the plan reference it was booked to, and the charge as booked in USD to two decimal places. A sentence naming that new entry reference is what indicates the charge is on the plan's billing history.

## Points of judgement

- The call books the figure it is given; the figure itself is worked out from the plan's records and this desk's published rules before the call.
- The entry is dated and cycled on today's date, whatever date the returned payment itself carries.
- The call books a charge; it does not move the plan's standing and does not restate the plan's balance.
